title: Choose a recovery plan for the situation
practice: Given an outage or disaster scenario, choose prevention, continuity and recovery measures. Explain the likely data loss, downtime and how you would test recovery.

title: Identify the real problems
practice: Summarize an unfamiliar case in your own words. Separate stated facts from assumptions and prioritize the problems you need to solve.

title: Compare feasible alternatives
practice: Compare at least two plausible approaches against the same requirements. Explain their costs, advantages, risks and limitations rather than listing products.

title: Defend a solution and implementation plan
practice: Recommend an approach and explain the implementation order, people and resources needed, validation checks and rollback plan.

title: Apply technical knowledge to the case
practice: Explain why the networking and security choices fit this case. Check the addressing, access, capacity and recovery assumptions relevant to your proposal.

title: Organize the spoken recommendation
practice: Give a clear briefing that moves from the problem to alternatives, your recommendation, implementation and verification. Ask a listener to summarize your recommendation.

title: Deliver it clearly and confidently
practice: Record a run-through or ask someone to observe your pace, projection, posture and audience engagement. Identify one specific change for the next attempt.

title: Handle judge questions during delivery
practice: Have a partner interrupt with unfamiliar questions. Listen, clarify when needed, explain your reasoning and acknowledge uncertainty before returning to the briefing.

title: Open naturally
practice: Create your own greeting and opening, then move smoothly into discovering the customer's needs rather than reciting a generic script.

title: Discover needs and listen
practice: Role-play with someone whose answers you do not know in advance. Ask open questions, follow up and confirm what matters before recommending an offer.

title: Explain and demonstrate the offer
practice: Use your actual product or service to explain relevant benefits, evidence, costs and limits. Verify the claims and practise the demonstration with an offline fallback.

title: Respond to objections
practice: Ask a partner to vary concerns about price, suitability or risk. Clarify the concern, answer honestly and check whether your response addressed it.

title: Make an appropriate close
practice: Make a clear, timely request for the sale or an appropriate next step. Respond to the customer's answer without pressure or invented promises.

title: Build the relationship and follow through
practice: Practise a useful recap and follow-up agreement with a partner. Confirm responsibilities, timing and permission to contact them; do not promise customer loyalty.

title: Keep the presentation organized and on time
practice: Run your actual presentation aloud, including team handoffs if applicable. Check that a listener can follow the offer, costs and next step within the event timing.

title: Deliver with confidence and clarity
practice: Record a complete run-through and get feedback on pace, projection, posture and audience engagement. Practise recovering from a missed line or a demonstration problem.

title: Answer interactive questions
practice: Have a partner ask unpredictable questions during the pitch. Listen fully, answer the actual question, state factual limits and return naturally to the conversation.
